_meta.indication: Treatment of adult and pediatric patients with hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD), also known as sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (SOS), with renal or pulmonary dysfunction following hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT)

pivotal_trials.population: Adult and pediatric patients with severe hepatic VOD meeting Baltimore diagnostic criteria who also had multi-organ failure (pulmonary and/or renal dysfunction) following HSCT
pivotal_trials.n: 102 patients in the defibrotide arm and 32 historical controls
pivotal_trials.result: Day +100 survival was 38% (95% CI: 29, 48) in the defibrotide arm vs 25% (95% CI: 12, 43) in the historical control arm

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=10%) were hypotension, diarrhea, vomiting, nausea and epistaxis; most common serious adverse reactions were hypotension (11%) and pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage (7%). Hypotension occurred in 65 (37%), diarrhea 43 (24%), vomiting 31 (18%), nausea 28 (16%), epistaxis 24 (14%) of 176 patients.
target_moa: Mechanism not fully elucidated; defibrotide sodium enhances plasmin enzymatic activity to hydrolyze fibrin clots and, in vitro, increases t-PA and thrombomodulin and decreases vWF and PAI-1 expression, reducing endothelial cell activation and increasing EC-mediated fibrinolysis
modality: Oligonucleotide (polydisperse mixture of predominately single-stranded polydeoxyribonucleotide sodium salts derived from porcine intestinal tissue)

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee

orphan_indication.text: Orphan designation for defibrotide for the treatment of hepatic VOD, granted May 21, 2003

summary.text: NDA 208114 (received July 31, 2015) was reviewed under priority review with an orphan drug designation granted for defibrotide for hepatic VOD; it was granted regular (full) approval based on Study 2005-01 and supportive studies, and was not referred to an advisory committee.
